heading: Shapiro-Wilk Test
text: also use statistical test check normality. important remember though test can bit unreliable large small samples.code little trickier need create separate objects group.use dollar sign $ point R particular column. example, using shapiro.test(helmet$BART) saying run Shapiro Test helmet data set specific column called BARTFor test, want non-significant p-value. means data roughly normally distributed. p-value significant, issue indicates data might normally distributed (cautious particularly large [80+] small sample).reporting Shapiro-Wilk test, just need report test statistics (w = XX) p-value. example look like:W = 0.98, p = .875
code:
#first create an object with only cap data
cap <- data %>%
  filter(condition == "cap")
#then run the test
shapiro.test(cap$BART)
#first create an object with only helmet data
helmet <- data %>%
  filter(condition == "helmet")
#then run the test
shapiro.test(helmet$BART)

heading: 2.7 Run the t-Test and Effect Size
text: t.test() t-test function.BART ~ condition formula, essentially DV ~ IVvar.equal = FALSE means get Welch’s version t-test. set =TRUE ’ll get Student’s t-test instead.alternative = "two-sided" relates alternative hypothesis. set non-directional hypothesis.
code:
#t.test code
t.test(BART ~ condition, data, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")
#effect size
cohens_d(data, BART ~ condition, var.equal = FALSE)
